subject: research/simdesign-pocketmesh
professional: a senior finite-element stress analyst / computational-mechanics researcher (mesh-convergence and solution verification practice: ASME V&V 20, Roache's grid convergence index, stress recovery); first checks: is there an analytic baseline the FE must approach, does the reported stress measure converge, are the scan numbers reproducible, and does the headline (pockets are a mesh artefact) survive the obvious alternative reading (the whole feasible set is collapsing)

evidence.correctness: Every number reproduces and the headline survives an independent analytic check. (1) Re-ran the full 372-point scan in a scratch copy (`cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/bfc40cd0-35aa-5329-b7a8-571e88aa5cb8/scratchpad/simdesign-pocketmesh/copy && /usr/bin/python3.13 experiments/meshscan.py`, 8.2 s wall on 4 cores): 0 feasibility mismatches, max |d peak| = 0 against the committed meshscan.json, meshscan.txt byte-identical. (2) Independent elementary-beam floor (`/usr/bin/python3.13 -I /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/bfc40cd0-35aa-5329-b7a8-571e88aa5cb8/scratchpad/simdesign-pocketmesh/beam.py`, no subject import): in the uniform vertical arm the extreme-fibre stress is 6F(L-w/2)/(b w^2) + F/(b w), which equals the 100 MPa limit at exactly w* = 15.000 mm (F = 100 N, L = 80, b = 2). The h = 2.5 'pockets' at w = 14.4-14.9 mm sit where beam theory already gives 102.8-108.8 MPa in the plain arm, so they must be discretisation artefacts, which is the README's reading; every h = 1.5 feasible w (15.6-16.0) is above w*. (3) The FE engine approaches that beam value: max centroid von Mises in the mid-arm band (y 40-55) at w = 15.0, r = 12 rises 88.1 -> 98.4 MPa from h = 2.5 to 0.75 against 100.0 analytic (`/usr/bin/python3.13 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/bfc40cd0-35aa-5329-b7a8-571e88aa5cb8/scratchpad/simdesign-pocketmesh/fecheck.py /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/bfc40cd0-35aa-5329-b7a8-571e88aa5cb8/scratchpad/simdesign-pocketmesh/copy/src`); at w = 15.4 it is 91.6 against 94.7. (4) Tip deflection 0.383 mm at w = 15 vs 0.452 mm Castigliano centreline-frame estimate (FE 15% stiffer, as expected from the rigid corner block); the 4 mm limit never binds. README values 105.8 / 100.2 / 92.1 MPa (h = 2.5, r = 12) and r = 10 h = 1.5 pattern 15.7, 15.8, 16.0 with 15.9 failing all match meshscan.json.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: '5 tests, a few seconds' (5 passed in 1.19 s); 'meshscan.py ... under a minute' (8.2 s); '372 points' (3 h x 4 r x 31 w = 372, counted in the JSON); the results table (all 12 rows match meshscan.txt); 'pockets reported by simdesign-gaugebasins reproduced here at h = 2.5' (r = 10: 14.6, 14.7; r = 12: 14.8; r = 14: 14.4, 14.9, identical to research/simdesign-gaugebasins/experiments/wscan.txt). experiments/wscan.py and figure.py exist; wscan.txt is not committed but is not claimed. No TODOs or stubs. Everything the README says was done runs end to end.
evidence.verification: `cd research/simdesign-pocketmesh && /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`: 5 passed, 60 warnings, 1.19 s. Two tests only check rule constants; the FE tests assert a bool type, peak > 0, infeasibility far from the boundary, and fine/coarse within a factor of two. No test pins a stress against a reference. Four mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 survived (stress limit x1.1 at dfm.py:131; shear stress doubled at model.py:128; load x1.2 at model.py:113), 1 caught (MAX_SLENDER 8 -> 7 at dfm.py:23, which makes the w = 15.8 test point rule-infeasible). A 20% error in the load or 10% in the limit moves the whole feasible boundary that the paper is about and no test notices.
evidence.craft: Read model.py, dfm.py, measures.py, optimise.py, meshscan.py, tests. Short and readable, units stated. Defects: the engine is a verbatim copy of simdesign-gaugebasins (`diff -q` on model, dfm, measures, optimise: identical), itself copied down a chain of simdesign-* projects, so a fix must be made many times; dead code at model.py:105-107 (`... if False else None`, and an unused `fb`); package docstring at __init__.py:1 describes the DFM rule module, not this project; meshscan.py:39-40 writes files without closing them; pytest not declared in pyproject.toml; tests import via sys.path insertion; 60 skfem DeprecationWarnings per test run. Acceptable research code, not reviewer-clean.
evidence.claims: README numbers all trace to experiments/meshscan.txt / meshscan.json (checked above). AI assistance, 'stylised', 'preliminary', 'Simulated results only' and a Limitations section are present (README:3, :35-38), and the README says plainly that h = 1.5 is not shown to be converged and that the mesh-noise reading was not tested. research/README.md:551 and research/_homepage/projects.json summaries match. The served page https://marisstella.app/research/simdesign-pocketmesh/ returns 200 and carries 'preliminary' (11x) and 'AI assistance'. Soft omission, not an overclaim: the README never says the feasible window is capped at w = 16.0 mm by the slenderness rule (dfm.py:23, w/b <= 8), so 'the boundary moves up' reads as a moving edge when it is a window shrinking against a hard cap.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it: the scan reruns bit-identically in seconds. But as a research step it is thin. The deferred 'next step' (h = 1.0) costs seconds: probing w = 15.6-16.0 at r = 10 and 14 on h = 1.0 gives 0 of 10 feasible, and on h = 0.75 1 of 10 (w = 16.0, r = 14, 99.47 MPa) (`/usr/bin/python3.13 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/bfc40cd0-35aa-5329-b7a8-571e88aa5cb8/scratchpad/simdesign-pocketmesh/finer.py /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/bfc40cd0-35aa-5329-b7a8-571e88aa5cb8/scratchpad/simdesign-pocketmesh/copy/src`, 5.8 s), i.e. the gauge-2 feasible set essentially vanishes, a stronger and different conclusion from 'the boundary moves up'; a later slug (research/simdesign-meshconverge) found the same. The analytic beam floor (w* = 15.000) answers the project's question (are the pockets artefacts?) without any mesh study. Nearest prior work: standard FE solution verification (Roache 1998 grid convergence index; ASME V&V 20-2009) and stress-concentration handbooks (Peterson's), none cited. One micro-question per slug, contrary to the programme model in research/CLAUDE.md.
evidence.domain: Against FE verification practice: (a) no analytic or handbook baseline, though the plain-arm beam stress gives a hard lower bound of w* = 15.0 mm; (b) peak stress is sampled at P2 element centroids (model.py:121-131), which sit inside the section and under-read surface stress by roughly 2d/w on a coarse mesh, the likely mechanism of the pockets; a reviewer would expect nodal/surface recovery (Zienkiewicz-Zhu SPR) or extrapolation; (c) three meshes from an unstructured grid-plus-Delaunay mesher that re-meshes as w changes, with no Richardson/GCI estimate, and a peak that is non-monotone in h (w = 15.0, r = 12: 105.8, 100.7, 112.4, 116.1, 117.4 MPa at h = 2.5, 2.0, 1.5, 1.0, 0.75, my run); (d) feasibility decided by a hard threshold on an unconverged, possibly singular peak at the fillet tangent point. The README states (c) and (d) as limits, which keeps it honest, but a senior analyst would not sign off the method as a way to locate a feasible boundary.

defects.what: No test pins an FE output against a reference: a 20% load error, a doubled shear stress and a 10% looser stress limit all leave the 5 tests green, though each moves the feasible boundary the project is about. A test that the mid-arm stress at w=15 approaches the beam value 100 MPa would catch all three.

No analytic baseline: elementary beam theory puts the plain-arm extreme-fibre stress at exactly 100 MPa at w = 15.000 mm, so the h = 2.5 pockets (14.4-14.9 mm, 102.8-108.8 MPa by beam theory) are artefacts without any mesh study, and any converged feasible w must exceed 15.0. The README argues it only from mesh trends.

The feasible window is capped above at w = 16.0 mm by the slenderness rule (w/b <= 8), which the README never states; read with that cap, 'the boundary moves up' is a window collapsing (h = 1.0: 0 of 10 points at r = 10, 14 feasible; h = 0.75: 1 of 10), a stronger conclusion the deferred next step would have found in seconds.

Peak stress is sampled at P2 element centroids, which lie inside the section and under-read surface stress on coarse meshes (the likely mechanism of the pockets); no surface/nodal recovery or Richardson/GCI estimate, and the peak is non-monotone in h.
Dead code: `fb = ... if False else None` and an unused `fb` from basis.boundary.
Engine (model, dfm, measures, optimise) is a verbatim copy of simdesign-gaugebasins and earlier simdesign-* slugs; fixes must be repeated across the chain.
Package docstring describes the DFM rule module ('Design-for-manufacture rules for a parametric L-bracket: FDM, CNC routing, ...'), not this project.
pytest used by tests but not declared; meshscan.py writes meshscan.txt/json with open() never closed.

verdict: A small, honest, fully reproducible mesh-refinement scan: the 372-point scan reruns bit-identically in 8 s, every README number traces to meshscan.json, and the headline (the h = 2.5 mm feasible pockets below 15.4 mm vanish at h = 1.5 mm) is right and is confirmed by an independent beam-theory floor of w* = 15.000 mm, below which the plain arm alone exceeds 100 MPa. It misses the bar on verification (3 of 4 seeded bugs in load, shear stress and limit survive the 5 tests) and falls short of a senior FE analyst's method: no analytic baseline, centroid-sampled peak stress, no convergence estimate, and an unmentioned slenderness cap at w = 16.0 mm that turns 'the boundary moves up' into 'the feasible set collapses' (0 of 10 probed points feasible at h = 1.0), a finding the deferred next step would have produced in seconds.
